status: Proposed; synthetic data; not implemented or user-tested

pages.title: An administrative overview with an explicit boundary
pages.description: Desktop · A coherent extension of Quiet precision. Aggregate work usage leads; personal histories and public rankings stay outside this surface.

pages.title: People administration is separate from usage accounting
pages.description: Desktop · Invite, change access and resolve lifecycle states without adding a performance score or an activity feed to the roster.

pages.title: A named drilldown that explains its purpose
pages.description: Desktop · This is a proposed cost-allocation capability. A self view is a different authorization path, not a filter over all members.

pages.title: Switch scope before loading data
pages.description: Desktop · Keep published profiles, private workspaces and community navigation visibly distinct. Clear the previous scope before requesting the next.

pages.title: Invitations disclose access before acceptance
pages.description: Desktop and mobile · The proposal adds invitee-bound, expiring invitations for private workspaces; current community invitations retain their own contract.

pages.title: Membership lifecycle with explicit consequences
pages.description: Desktop dialogs · Suspensions, removals and owner transfer are server-authorized state transitions. A disabled button is never the enforcement boundary.

pages.title: Mobile uses the same scope and permission rules
pages.description: Four mobile states · Stacked records replace dense tables. Controls stay reachable, labels remain visible, and sensitive operations retain a review step.

pages.title: State design carries the trust contract
pages.description: Desktop and mobile patterns · These states are proposed specifications. Existing loading, empty and failure primitives should be extended, not erased.

pages.title: Make access and retention reviewable
pages.description: Desktop policy panel · A member can understand who sees their attributed usage. Administration, aggregate review and named accounting remain independent.
